# ZAP alert filter. Tab-separated: <rule: # ZAP runs weekly against the live site from a GitHub-hosted runner
# (.github/workflows/dast.yaml). Findings go to code scanning as SARIF, never to
# the public log, an issue or an artifact.
# WHAT GATES: any HIGH alert, by count (scripts/zap_sarif.py, then the gate
# step). The accepted baseline is zero HIGH. A HIGH that is accepted gets an
# IGNORE row below with its reason; IGNORE rows are dropped before the count,
# so every HIGH that reaches the gate is new. Medium and below report only.
# FAIL rows are not used: the HIGH count is the gate.
# The four header rules are WARN because the shared Gateway sets no response
# headers yet (no ResponseHeaderModifier filter in the repo).
# scripts/tls-check.sh checks the same four headers, and hard-fails on
# reachability, the http -> https redirect and certificate expiry.
# TO PROMOTE THE HEADERS TO A GATE, in one commit:
#   1. add the ResponseHeaderModifier filter in infrastructure/gateway
#   2. set STRICT_HEADERS=1 on the tls step in dast.yaml
# Only rules with a stated reason belong here. Everything not listed keeps its
# default behaviour, which for a baseline scan is WARN.
# Find a rule ID in the ZAP HTML report, or:
#   https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
